response: {"turns":[{"id":"M1:T1","text":"Okay, let's get started. Thanks for joining. This is the kickoff, so the first of 3 meetings on the functional and non-functional requirements for the VCD. Today I mainly want to get the big picture."},{"id":"M1:T2","text":"Good to see everyone. Nice to start a week with something fresh."},{"id":"M1:T3","text":"Sure, so some background. Using ICT to get interoperability in public procurement really matters for the Lisbon objectives, the idea of becoming the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world, that's from EC 2005. But the eProcurement infrastructure we have across Europe right now just isn't fit for that. The market is very fragmented and there's a lack of interoperability. And governments are the biggest buyer in the EU, they purchase at roughly 15-20% of GDP, according to the Ministerial Declaration from 2005."},{"id":"M1:T4","text":"So on the major features, requirements and quality attributes, I'll just jump in. I think maybe we need a governing model defined, so we can deploy the infrastructure and keep its state and sustainability going over time. I'm not sure it's strictly mandatory, but it'd be good."},{"id":"M1:T5","text":"And it'd be nice if the commonly approved national mappings were accessible to the different stakeholders, especially economic operators, contracting authorities and national VCD service providers. Maybe that's a must, I'm not totally sure."},{"id":"M1:T6","text":"Which means the criteria might need to be redefined iteratively, depending on what specific mappings turn out to give us."},{"id":"M1:T7","text":"Right, okay."},{"id":"M1:T8","text":"And then that mapping has to be implemented in the pre-VCD mapping tool, like in the use-case diagram in Figure 9. So a list of criteria to be matched gets submitted to whatever entity does the mapping."},{"id":"M1:T9","text":"Got it."},{"id":"M1:T10","text":"The question I keep coming back to, and maybe we don't have to pin it down now, is by which technical means the mapping actually gets provided..."},{"id":"M1:T11","text":"Mm, go on."},{"id":"M1:T12","text":"So that depends on which pilot solution we pick. The simplest version, no technical support at all, could be handing out mapping tables on paper, one time. Another option is web-based access to a system that does the mapping by querying an underlying database holding the mapping table. More advanced would be automated processing of the mapping based on the relevant criteria, and then the contracting authority has to specify those in a dedicated electronic format. And the higher maturity levels in this vision, stage 2-4, can also use the mapping service to retrieve the mapping information."},{"id":"M1:T13","text":"Which of those are you actually leaning towards for the pilot?"},{"id":"M1:T14","text":"Hard to say yet. It really depends on how things shape up, we'll see."},{"id":"M1:T15","text":"On maintainability, the mapping has to be easy to maintain, which could matter if the legal basis changes on national—"},{"id":"M1:T16","text":"Sorry, quick one, are you still sharing your screen?"},{"id":"M1:T17","text":"Oh, no, I stopped. Let me sort that out after."},{"id":"M1:T18","text":"Anyway, national or European level. We need a formal procedure for how changes get applied to the system. And we also have to define an organisation or institution that governs the change management process."},{"id":"M1:T19","text":"Let's talk about accessibility of the mapping facility. Who needs to get at it?"},{"id":"M1:T20","text":"Every national service provider offering a VCD, so stage 2-4, plus all the other relevant key stakeholders like economic operators, contracting authorities and certifiers, they must all be able to pull the latest mapping information from the mapping facility."}]}
